learn.title: Learn Concepts

topics.title: Introduction

content.text: So far we have learned second declension nouns, which have a stem ending in omicron, and first declension nouns, which have a stem ending in either alpha or eta. Third declension nouns have stems which end in a consonant. When the endings are added, the consonant will go through various predictable transformations.

Unlike the first and second declensions, which build their forms from the nominative, third declension nouns will be built from the genitive. Thus, in the third declension, you must memorize the genitive form of the noun.
To find the stem of third declension nouns, take the ος off of the genitive form.

content.text: The following consonants in the voiced and unvoiced columns are called "stops" because of the way the air flow stops when pronouncing them. The aspirates are fricatives. These letters will be transformed when the sigma of the third declension is added. (Mounce, p. 78)

content.text: The consonants (labials, velars, dentals) change in the following ways when the sigma ending is added. The two letters contract into one.

content._greek_note: Notation, not taps (no clips; see Key Letter Box.)

content.text: Nu drops out when followed by a sigma.
An unvoiced consonant is one where the voice box is not used (e.g. the "p" in Peter).
A voiced consonant is one where the voiced box is used (e.g. the "g" in grin).
An aspirate consonant is one where the sound is made by the aspiration of air out of the mouth (e.g. the "ph" in phone).
A labial is a sound like "b" in "boat" made using the lips.
A velar is a sound like "k" in "kitchen" made using the palate and tongue.
A dental is a sound like "t" in "top" made using the teeth and tongue.

topics.title: Introduction

content.text: We will learn four paradigms which are typical of third declension nouns. The adjective πᾶς, πᾶσα, πᾶν (each, all) will be examined as a 3-1-3 adjective (third-first-third declension).
Take the ος ending off of the genitive form to find the stem. In the nominative singular a sigma is added to the stem causing the final consonant of the stem to change.

items.greek: καὶ χάρις θεοῦ ἦν ἐπ' αὐτό
options: and the grace of God was upon him
and the God of grace was upon him
and grace was of God upon him
items.answer: and the grace of God was upon him

items.greek: χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν
options: for grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus
your grace and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
items.answer: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ

items.greek: χάριτι δὲ θεοῦ εἰμι ὅ εἰμι
options: but the grace of God is what it is
but by the grace of God I am what I am
but grace is of God which is
items.answer: but by the grace of God I am what I am

items.greek: ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ τοῦ
options: grace is from the Lord Jesus Christ with his spirit
by the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ with your spirit
the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit
items.answer: the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit

items.greek: ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ
options: the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you
the graces of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you
by the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ I am with all of you
items.answer: the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you

options: and God is all grace
and every grace is from God
and the God of all grace
items.answer: and the God of all grace

items.greek: καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν
options: and the two shall become one flesh
and they shall be two of one flesh
and for one flesh they shall be two
items.answer: and the two shall become one flesh

items.greek: ἡ γὰρ σὰρξ ἐπιθυμεῖ κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος
options: for of the flesh come desires against the Spirit
for the flesh desires against the Spirit
for by the flesh come desires against the Spirit

items.greek: ὃς ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ
options: who in the days of his flesh
whose flesh in those days
in those days his flesh

items.greek: ὅτι πᾶν τὸ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ , ἡ ἐπιθυμία τῆς σαρκὸς
options: for lust and flesh are in all the world
for all that is in the world is lust, flesh
for all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh

items.greek: ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐν σαρκὶ ἀλλὰ ἐν πνεύματι
options: but you are not in the Spirit but in the flesh
but you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit
but the flesh is not of the Spirit
items.answer: but you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit

items.greek: ὅτι πνεῦμα σάρκα καὶ ὀστέα οὐκ ἔχει
options: for a spirit does not have flesh and bones
for a spirit of flesh does not have bones
for flesh and bones do not have a spirit
items.answer: for a spirit does not have flesh and bones

items.greek: ὑμεῖς κατὰ τὴν σάρκα κρίνετε, ἐγὼ οὐ κρίνω
options: you judge according to the flesh, I judge no one
your flesh judges, but I judge no one
you judge my flesh, but I judge no one
